quote: keep tests deterministic, with no sleeps, timer cushions, retries, or regenerated goldens as correctness mechanisms.
statement: In all tests, code must not use sleeps, timer cushions, retries, or regenerated goldens as correctness mechanisms; tests must be deterministic.

quote: Validate by who can author a value: public caller input, third-party callback results, and external data once at the boundary; trust package-owned output and prove it at the producer.
statement: In package source, code must validate public caller input, third-party callback results and external data once at the entry boundary, and must not re-validate package-owned output on internal paths.

quote: Never justify a runtime guard with a test that forges a value no production caller can supply.
statement: In tests, code must not forge values no production caller can supply in order to justify a runtime guard.

quote: For TSL typing changes, start from `packages/glyph/tests/types/tsl-*.test.ts`.
statement: For TSL typing changes, work should start from the focused type regressions in packages/glyph/tests/types/tsl-*.test.ts.

quote: Model a closed set of alternatives with an enum or discriminated union. Make invalid combinations unrepresentable when the model stays local and inexpensive.
statement: In all code, a closed set of alternatives should be modeled with an enum or discriminated union rather than combinations of flags.

quote: Keep functions total over their declared domain and make expected failure explicit.
statement: In all code, functions should be total over their declared domain and expected failure must be explicit.

quote: Retain typed semantic state until the presentation edge. Never recover state by parsing labels, messages, class names, or other display strings.
statement: In all code, state must not be recovered by parsing labels, error messages, class names or other display strings; typed semantic state is retained until the presentation edge.

quote: Use classes only for identity, lifecycle, cleanup, encapsulated mutation, or stateful caches. Prefer data and functions otherwise;
statement: In all code, classes should be used only for identity, lifecycle, cleanup, encapsulated mutation or stateful caches; otherwise plain data and functions are preferred.

quote: do not introduce inheritance for variant modeling.
statement: In all code, class inheritance must not be introduced to model variants.

quote: Preserve behavior with independent invariants and oracles, not snapshots derived only from the implementation being changed.
statement: In tests for optimizations, behavior should be preserved with independent invariants and oracles rather than snapshots derived from the implementation being changed.

quote: Do not couple unrelated packages merely because a few lines look alike.
statement: Across packages, code must not be shared between unrelated packages merely because a few lines look alike.

quote: Keep one canonical optimized artifact and one owner for generated contracts. Consumers reference that owner instead of copying bytes or offsets.
statement: In all code, consumers of generated contracts must reference the single owning artifact instead of copying its bytes or offsets.

quote: Keep portable Wasm crates `no_std + alloc` where their capability permits it. Host-only tools, compression, fixture inspection, and oracle generation stay behind explicit features or binaries.
statement: In portable Wasm Rust crates, code must stay no_std + alloc where possible, and host-only tooling must be behind explicit cargo features or binaries.

quote: prefer one shared implementation with that branch over const-generic or duplicated pipelines unless a representative end-to-end benchmark proves the duplication wins
statement: In Rust kernels, one shared implementation with a coarse branch should be preferred over const-generic or duplicated pipelines unless benchmarks justify duplication.

quote: Use maintained font, shaping, raster, Unicode, and container libraries instead of project-owned parsers when a suitable implementation exists.
statement: In Rust and TypeScript, code should use maintained font, shaping, raster, Unicode and container libraries rather than project-owned parsers.

quote: Use error enums and exhaustive matches for operational failure and closed state. Convert enums and newtypes to C/Serde primitives only at the boundary.
statement: In Rust code, operational failure and closed state must use error enums with exhaustive matches, converting enums/newtypes to C or Serde primitives only at the boundary.

quote: Add `#[repr(transparent)]` newtypes when primitive values from distinct units, identities, generations, ownership domains, or coordinate spaces could plausibly be mixed.
statement: In Rust code, primitives from distinct units, identities, generations, ownership domains or coordinate spaces that could be mixed should be wrapped in #[repr(transparent)] newtypes.

quote: Do not use `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, unchecked indexing, or truncating casts as error control flow on reusable production or caller-controlled paths.
statement: In reusable production Rust paths, code must not use unwrap, expect, panic!, unchecked indexing or truncating casts as error control flow (tests and build scripts excepted).

quote: Use checked aggregation and `try_reserve`/`try_reserve_exact` before caller-derived growth where stable Rust permits it; publish state only after all fallible work succeeds.
statement: In Rust code, caller-derived growth must use checked arithmetic and try_reserve/try_reserve_exact, and state must be published only after all fallible work succeeds.

quote: Keep `unsafe` blocks small and adjacent to a `SAFETY` explanation covering ownership, range, lifetime, reentrancy, and concurrency assumptions.
statement: In Rust code, every unsafe block must be small and have an adjacent SAFETY comment covering ownership, range, lifetime, reentrancy and concurrency.

quote: Own allocations in the module that releases them. Validate exact pointer/length or handle identity and test forged ranges, repeated release, overflow, and stale ownership.
statement: In Rust/Wasm memory code, allocations must be owned by the module that releases them, with exact pointer/length or handle validation.

quote: Repository-authored TypeScript and JavaScript use the single root Oxfmt configuration ... Package-local formatter policies are not allowed;
statement: In the repository, packages must not add package-local formatter configurations; the single root .oxfmtrc.json applies.

quote: Prefer discriminated unions for protocol, lifecycle, result, and exclusive option states. Use exhaustive checks when a new variant must force downstream review.
statement: In TypeScript, protocol, lifecycle, result and exclusive option states should be discriminated unions with exhaustive checks.

quote: Use branded primitives for opaque handles and hashes when equal representations have different identities.
statement: In TypeScript, opaque handles and hashes should use branded primitive types.

quote: Keep untyped boundary data `unknown`. A cast, `as Partial<T>`, object check, or property-presence check is not validation.
statement: In TypeScript, untyped boundary data must be typed unknown, and casts such as as Partial<T> or property-presence checks must not be used as validation.
scope: all TypeScript source at trust boundaries

quote: Do not treat a package, config, registry, or callback boundary as a reason to erase types. Preserve associated types through generic inference when a runtime value ... already witnesses their relationship.
statement: In TypeScript, types must not be erased to unknown/any at package, config, registry or callback boundaries when a runtime witness such as GlyphConfig already ties them; associated types are preserved via generic inference.

quote: Do not make consumers reconstruct relationships with `Any*` types, `unknown`, explicit generic arguments, or corrective casts.
statement: In TypeScript registries and their consumers, code must not reconstruct type relationships with Any* types, unknown, explicit generic arguments or corrective casts; registration packages every needed operation while the concrete type is known.

quote: return `value is T` only when every promised part of `T` is proven;
statement: In TypeScript, a type predicate returning value is T must prove every promised part of T; a classifier that proves nothing useful returns boolean.
scope: type guards in all TypeScript source

quote: use `asserts value is T` for throwing validation; return a normalized `T` when validation also copies, defaults, or canonicalizes.
statement: In TypeScript, throwing validators should be typed asserts value is T, and validators that copy/default/canonicalize should return a normalized T.

quote: For an unknown object, first prove it is a non-null, non-array object, then prove every property the returned type promises or the caller consumes. Use `"key" in value` when presence matters and `Object.hasOwn(value, "key")` when inherited properties must not satisfy the contract
statement: In TypeScript validation of unknown objects, code must first prove non-null non-array object, then each property; use 'in' for presence and Object.hasOwn when inherited properties must not count.

quote: Name structural predicates honestly. `isNonArrayObject` is appropriate for the one fact it proves. Use `isPlainObject` only when prototypes are restricted. Do not introduce a generic `isRecord` that implies domain properties exist.
statement: In TypeScript, structural predicates must be named for what they prove (isNonArrayObject; isPlainObject only when prototypes are restricted); a generic isRecord helper must not be introduced.
scope: type predicates in all TypeScript source

quote: If a consumer needs only part of a wire value, define a narrower wire type. Do not make a predicate promise a richer public or domain type than it validates.
statement: In TypeScript, a predicate must not promise a richer public or domain type than it validates; define a narrower wire type instead.

quote: Classify trust by who can author a value, not by whether it crosses a module, package, Worker, language, or Wasm boundary. ... Keep pointer, range, capacity, and allocation checks required for memory safety.
statement: In package code, package-produced Worker/Wasm messages must be trusted without semantic re-validation, while pointer, range, capacity and allocation checks for memory safety must be kept.

quote: State whether JSON-facing APIs accept only materialized JSON or intentionally apply `JSON.stringify` coercions. Bound depth and size, reject cycles and invalid values where programmatic input can exceed parsed-JSON guarantees
statement: In JSON-facing public APIs, code must bound depth and size and reject cycles and invalid values for programmatic input, documenting whether JSON.stringify coercions apply.

quote: Do not add schema walks, canonicality scans, duplicate-ID searches, relationship validation, deep equality, or type-recovery branches to shaping, layout, rendering, serialization, projection, or other internal paths.
statement: In internal shaping, layout, rendering, serialization and projection paths, code must not add schema walks, canonicality scans, duplicate-ID searches, relationship validation, deep equality or type-recovery branches over package-owned values.

quote: Before writing a negative test, prove a production caller can reach the tested state. If only a test can forge the value, delete the proposed runtime guard and test the package-owned producer instead.
statement: In tests, negative tests must target states a production caller can reach; an internal source file imported only by a test is not a caller boundary.

quote: Treat a renderer-side reconciliation state machine as an architecture review trigger.
statement: In renderer integrations, a renderer-side reconciliation state machine requires architecture review with correctness tests and performance evidence.

quote: Renderer integrations implement the public `GlyphConfig` contract; do not give a built-in renderer a second core API.
statement: In renderer integrations (three, typegpu), code must implement the public GlyphConfig contract and must not get a second private core API.

quote: Keep the bridge package-private, and do not expose internal state or add forwarding modules merely to satisfy directory-layer linting.
statement: In companion entries such as React, the construction/identity bridge must stay package-private and forwarding modules must not be added merely to satisfy directory-layer lint rules.

quote: Begin cleanup scope before the first resource acquisition. Track each successful allocation, listener, Worker, handle, or publication independently and release it after any later failure.
statement: In resource-acquiring code, cleanup scope must begin before the first acquisition and each allocation, listener, Worker, handle or publication must be released after any later failure.

quote: Use React 19 async primitives and let the React Compiler optimize ordinary component code.
statement: In React components, code should use React 19 async primitives and rely on the React Compiler instead of manual memoization.

quote: Derive values during render when they are pure. Do not use an effect to mirror props/state, repair event flow, or implement derivation.
statement: In React components, pure values must be derived during render and effects must not mirror props/state, repair event flow or implement derivation.

quote: Use `useEffectEvent` for non-reactive effect callbacks that need current values. Do not use render-time refs as an effect dependency workaround.
statement: In React components, non-reactive effect callbacks must use useEffectEvent, and render-time refs must not be used to work around effect dependencies.

quote: Preserve semantic values as typed props through the component boundary; derive labels and visual tone together at the final render site.
statement: In React components, semantic values should pass as typed props and labels/visual tone should be derived at the final render site, not passed as preformatted strings.

quote: Keep the React layer thin. Core lifecycle and capability state belong in the framework-neutral package rather than a parallel component-only model.
statement: In the React adapter, core lifecycle and capability state must live in the framework-neutral package, not a parallel component-only model.

quote: Prefer official conformance suites, independent implementations, exact artifact authentication, and externally derived invariants over implementation-shaped assertions.
statement: In tests, assertions should come from conformance suites, independent implementations or external invariants rather than implementation-shaped expectations.

quote: Retain a test only when a reader can name a realistic production behavior change that makes it fail. Delete tests whose only failure requires changing their own mock, expectation, or copied implementation
statement: In tests, a test must fail on a realistic production behavior change; tests that fail only when their own mock, expectation or copied implementation changes must be deleted.

quote: Prefer the highest-order deterministic test that proves an invariant, keeping lower-order coverage only for a distinct boundary, failure mode, public type contract, conformance oracle, or measured hot-path property.
statement: In tests, the highest-order deterministic test proving an invariant should be preferred over duplicated lower-order tests.

quote: Do not use sleeps, timer cushions, arbitrary retries, frame counts, or random luck as correctness mechanisms. A live browser/GPU lane must use causal completion signals and negative controls.
statement: In tests and live browser/GPU probes, code must not use sleeps, timer cushions, retries or frame counts as correctness; it must wait on causal completion signals and include negative controls.

quote: Review generated outputs through their generator, inputs, provenance, deterministic regeneration check, and conformance suite. Do not hand-style generated source.
statement: In generated source (src/generated/**), code must not be hand-edited or hand-styled; changes go through the generator.

quote: Add comments for non-obvious ownership, safety, protocol, performance, or mathematical invariants; match surrounding comment density instead of applying a blanket comment rule.
statement: In all code, comments should explain non-obvious ownership, safety, protocol, performance or mathematical invariants and match surrounding density.

quote: Give every public TypeScript declaration concise TSDoc that states its contract and any non-obvious cost or lifetime behavior.
statement: In TypeScript, every public (exported) declaration must have concise TSDoc stating its contract and any non-obvious cost or lifetime behavior.

quote: Preserve public signatures unless correctness, measured performance, or a seriously misleading name supplies strong evidence for a change.
statement: In public APIs, signatures should be preserved unless correctness, measured performance or a seriously misleading name justifies change.

quote: This standard does not require a newtype for every primitive, an abstraction for every repeated expression, a type guard for every object check, `.get()` for every proven index, classes to model alternatives, zero allocations, or zero comments.
statement: Deliberate non-rules: code is not required to newtype every primitive, abstract every repetition, type-guard every object check, use .get() for every proven index, or have zero allocations or comments.

statement: In apps/r3f-hello-world/**, code must not deep-import three/src/*.

quote: eslint/no-restricted-imports patterns: three/addons/*
statement: In apps/r3f-hello-world/**, code must not import three/addons/*.

quote: eslint/no-restricted-imports patterns: three/examples/*
statement: In apps/r3f-hello-world/**, code must not import three/examples/*.

quote: ignore.overrides: [{ files: [src/benchmark/paragraph-layout-digest.ts], rules: [deslop/unused-export] }]
statement: In benches/src/benchmark/paragraph-layout-digest.ts, the react-doctor deslop/unused-export rule is turned off.

quote: supplyChain: { enabled: false }
statement: In benches/**, react-doctor supply-chain checks are disabled.

quote: Return the answer. `layout()` returns metrics. `glyphs()` returns the inspection. No `{ ok }` union, no nullable, no out-of-band error to consult afterwards.
statement: In engine calls, code must return the answer directly and must not return { ok } result unions, nullable results or out-of-band error state.

quote: Throw for input the language let them express but which has no meaning. ... Throw from the call, name the axis or the span or the offset, and let the stack point at the caller.
statement: In engine calls, well-typed but meaningless input (e.g. NaN size) must throw synchronously from the call with a message naming the axis, span or offset, not be clamped or silently accepted.

quote: Never return or proactively scan for a failure the caller cannot cause.
statement: In engine code, code must not return result values for or proactively scan for package defects a caller cannot cause.

quote: Never enter a broken state that outlives the call. A rejected frame must not leave the engine refusing work, recompiling an invalid frame at frame rate, or holding a latch a caller has to clear.
statement: In the engine, a rejected frame must not leave persistent broken state, frame-rate recompilation or a latch a caller must clear.

quote: Prefer a shape that cannot express the mistake over a check that catches it. Structural authoring beats offsets.
statement: In public API design, shapes that cannot express mistakes (structural txt/span authoring) should be preferred over offset ranges plus runtime checks.

quote: A value or type an application can encounter lives at the root. A renderer-neutral helper only an integrator calls lives on `/core`.
statement: In @pmndrs/glyph exports, application-encountered values and types must be exported from the root entry, and integrator-only renderer-neutral helpers (e.g. defineGlyphConfig) from /core.

quote: Internal engine, planner, wire, projection, and binding machinery has no public subpath.
statement: In packages/glyph/package.json exports, internal engine, planner, wire, projection and binding machinery must not be given a public subpath.

quote: Keep the core entry as static ESM re-exports of focused implementation modules so unused helpers remain tree-shakeable. Do not re-export those helpers from the root; each helper has one public home.
statement: In the /core entry, code must be static ESM re-exports of focused modules, and /core helpers must not be re-exported from the root entry.

quote: An integration may re-export a root name only when its own signatures use it
statement: In integration entries (/three, /react, /typegpu), a root name may be re-exported only when that integration's own signatures use it.

quote: A renderer type must not enter shared text vocabulary to make an integration convenient. ... Pushing a `THREE.Material` or GPU handle into renderer-neutral spans is the mistake this rule exists to prevent.
statement: In renderer-neutral text types, renderer types such as THREE.Material or GPU handles must not appear; renderer-specific types stay behind GlyphConfig schema/resolve/renderer.

quote: Every maintained function must satisfy all three inequalities: Cyclomatic Complexity < 22, Cognitive Complexity < 22, Halstead Difficulty < 80
statement: In maintained production functions, cyclomatic complexity must be < 22, cognitive complexity < 22 and Halstead difficulty < 80.
scope: maintained production functions (excluding generated, vendored, fixtures)

quote: Do not introduce a union merely to wrap one boolean, and do not copy the same state into a second controller.
statement: In TypeScript, a discriminated union must not be introduced merely to wrap one boolean, and the same state must not be copied into a second controller.

quote: For multi-step decisions, return a small discriminated outcome such as `reuse | create | unsupported` rather than stacking ternaries. Do not move branches into anonymous callbacks or chains of `some`, `filter`, and `map`
statement: In all code, multi-step decisions should return a small discriminated outcome instead of stacked ternaries, and branches must not be moved into anonymous callbacks or some/filter/map chains to lower metrics.

quote: The built-in decoder, Rust-plan mapper, buffer patcher, and transform synchronizer should retain indexed loops and borrowed views. ... Do not add validation for typed data returned by the Rust engine
statement: In the built-in decoder, Rust-plan mapper, buffer patcher and transform synchronizer, code should keep direct indexed loops and borrowed views and must not validate typed data returned by the Rust engine.

quote: Do not expose `AnyGlyphConfig` or another existential as the consumer's inference surface. Do not rebuild a concrete type with `as unknown as`, a caller-chosen generic, an explicit six-parameter `GlyphConfig<...>`, or a consumer cast.
statement: In TypeScript, AnyGlyphConfig or other existentials must not be exposed as the consumer inference surface, and concrete types must not be rebuilt with as unknown as, caller-chosen generics, explicit GlyphConfig<...> tuples or consumer casts.

quote: Do not add thin wrappers, one-line adapters, or forwarding classes to lower a caller's score.
statement: In all code, thin wrappers, one-line adapters or forwarding classes must not be added to lower a complexity score.

quote: Do not copy an optimized Rust table into TypeScript or materialize a second command hierarchy.
statement: In TypeScript, code must not copy an optimized Rust table or materialize a second command hierarchy.

quote: Do not replace a direct hot loop with generators, iterator-result allocation, or array combinators without measurement.
statement: In hot paths, direct loops must not be replaced with generators, iterator allocation or array combinators without measurement.

quote: Do not suppress a metric because the function is difficult. ... maintained exceptions require explicit user approval and a documented invariant.
statement: In maintained code, complexity metrics must not be suppressed without explicit approval and a documented invariant.

quote: Do not use type erasure to make a helper compile. If inference fails, repair the producer signature.
statement: In TypeScript, type erasure must not be used to make a helper compile; fix the producer signature instead.

quote: In an inference fixture, let the public factory call infer the value first and assert the result afterward. An explicit return annotation, `Any*` binding alias, generic argument, or corrective cast can make a broken inference path look green.
statement: In type-inference test fixtures, the public factory call must infer the value with no explicit return annotation, Any* alias, generic argument or corrective cast, then assert the result.

quote: React and R3F tests should assert Glyph behavior ... Do not test React's render count, effect ordering, hook internals, or StrictMode replay for their own sake.
statement: In React/R3F tests, assertions should target Glyph behavior and must not test React render counts, effect ordering, hook internals or StrictMode replay for their own sake.

quote: Derive expectations from authenticated fixtures, independent implementations, public measurements, or explicit contracts. Do not copy the production parser, mapper, range builder, or policy table into a helper and compare the two.
statement: In tests, production parsers, mappers, range builders or policy tables must not be copied into test helpers to compute expectations.

quote: When several closed variants have the same lifecycle and only their expected metadata differs, prefer one table-driven test with explicit per-variant expectations.
statement: In tests, closed variants sharing a lifecycle should be covered by one table-driven test with per-variant expectations rather than repeated files.

quote: Keep test names accountable to their assertions. A title that claims a value is hidden, a path is public, or a resource is released must contain an assertion that would fail if that exact contract regressed
statement: In tests, a test title's claim must be backed by an assertion that fails if that exact contract regresses.

quote: remove debug or entry/exit logging, replace vague TODOs with owned follow-up work, remove comments that merely narrate syntax, and reject catch blocks that only log and continue.
statement: In changed code, debug or entry/exit logging, vague TODOs, syntax-narrating comments and catch blocks that only log and continue should be removed.

quote: Do not import its blanket preferences for truthiness, explicit boolean comparisons, wildcard imports, or try/catch syntax.
statement: Deliberate non-rule: code is not required to follow blanket truthiness, explicit boolean comparison, wildcard-import or try/catch style preferences.

quote: canonical integrations must compile without `Any*`, `unknown`, explicit generic repair, or corrective casts
statement: In canonical integrations (three, example renderer), code must compile without Any* types, unknown, explicit generic repair or corrective casts.

quote: Tests may import such files to own a focused internal contract, but must not present that evidence as a public integration contract.
statement: In tests, imports of private src/core or dist/core files must not be presented as public integration contract evidence.

quote: Build typed node graphs with `three/tsl`; use `three/webgpu` for WebGPU renderer and classes.
statement: In TSL code, node graphs must be built from three/tsl and WebGPU renderer/classes imported from three/webgpu.

quote: Invoke an `Fn` when a node value is required: `Fn(() => expression)()`.
statement: In TSL code, an Fn must be invoked when a node value is required: Fn(() => expression)().

quote: Use TSL operations rather than JavaScript operators.
statement: In TSL node graphs, arithmetic must use TSL operations (add, mul, method chains) rather than JavaScript operators.

quote: Call `.toVar()` before mutation, then use `.assign()` or compound assignment methods.
statement: In TSL code, nodes must be converted with .toVar() before mutation and mutated with .assign() or compound assignment methods.

quote: Update runtime uniforms through `.value`; changing graph structure requires rebuilding the graph.
statement: In TSL code, runtime uniforms must be updated through .value rather than rebuilding the graph.

quote: Use `If`, `Loop`, and other TSL control nodes for runtime GPU control flow.
statement: In TSL code, runtime GPU control flow must use If, Loop and other TSL control nodes; JavaScript branches only select graph structure at build time.

quote: Await `renderer.init()` before the first WebGPU render or compute dispatch.
statement: In WebGPU code, renderer.init() must be awaited before the first render or compute dispatch.

quote: Keep node types intact. Do not cast to a broad `Node` or `unknown` merely to silence the compiler.
statement: In TSL code, node values must not be cast to broad Node or unknown merely to silence the compiler.

quote: Dispose render targets, textures, buffers, passes, and materials according to their owner. Restore renderer state around custom passes.
statement: In Three/TSL code, render targets, textures, buffers, passes and materials must be disposed by their owner, and renderer state restored around custom passes.

quote: Keep project code on the public `three/webgpu` and `three/tsl` barrels; do not add `customConditions` or a source-path import merely because an older workaround recommended it.
statement: In project code, Three.js must be imported only from the public three/webgpu and three/tsl barrels, without customConditions or three/src source-path imports.

quote: Use `import type` for type-only imports.
statement: In TypeScript, type-only imports must use import type.

quote: Avoid bare `Node`, `any`, or double casts: they erase useful operator and swizzle information.
statement: In TSL TypeScript, bare Node types, any and double casts should be avoided; use typed Node<'float'> etc.

quote: Avoid assigning `add` or `mul` to a narrower custom function type when an ordinary direct call communicates the same intent.
statement: In TSL code, add/mul should be called directly rather than assigned to narrower custom function types.

quote: Do not scatter `@ts-expect-error` through graph code. If one is unavoidable, make its reason and expected compiler error local
statement: In TSL graph code, @ts-expect-error must not be scattered; any unavoidable one must carry a local reason.

quote: Prefer `select`, `mix`, `step`, or `smoothstep` when they express the behavior clearly without control-flow divergence
statement: In TSL code, select, mix, step or smoothstep should be preferred over If when they express the behavior clearly.

quote: Do not reach through a texture node's `.value` to guess at a render-time attachment.
statement: In TSL post-processing code, a texture node's .value must not be accessed to guess a render-time attachment.

quote: Do not create parallel CPU and GPU buffers without an explicit synchronization reason.
statement: In TSL compute code, parallel CPU and GPU buffers must not be created without an explicit synchronization reason.

quote: Uninitialised variables: `let x;` is invalid - always initialise so the type can be inferred: `let x = d.f32(0)`.
statement: In TypeGPU 'use gpu' shader functions, variables must always be initialised (e.g. let x = d.f32(0)).

quote: runtime ternaries compile to WGSL `select` — both branches always evaluate, so branches must be side-effect-free and scalar/vector-valued (no structs/arrays/matrices; use `if`/`else` for those).
statement: In TypeGPU shader functions, runtime ternaries must have side-effect-free scalar/vector branches; use if/else for structs, arrays or matrices.

quote: Fragment output is always 4-component (`d.vec4f`; `d.vec4i`/`d.vec4u` for integer formats), even for fewer-channel formats.
statement: In TypeGPU fragment functions, the output must be a 4-component vector (d.vec4f / vec4i / vec4u) regardless of target format.

quote: Use pinned `ts-morph` for TypeScript and TSX migrations.
statement: In codemod recipes, TypeScript/TSX transforms must use the pinned ts-morph.

quote: For symbol renames, use the runner's `renameSymbol()` helper. It delegates identifiers to ts-morph's language service, scans actual comment trivia separately, and never renames string literals.
statement: In codemod recipes, symbol renames must use the runner's renameSymbol() helper and must not rename string literals.

quote: do not rename protocol values, persisted data, fixture identities, generated ABI names, or artifact paths because their spelling resembles an API symbol.
statement: In API renames, protocol values, persisted data, fixture identities, generated ABI names and artifact paths must not be renamed because they resemble the API symbol.

quote: Generated JavaScript, declarations, digests, and ABI files are regenerated through their owning workflow, never edited by the codemod.
statement: In codemod recipes, generated JavaScript, declarations, digests and ABI files must not be edited by the codemod.

quote: Recipes live under `codemods/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/` and are applied in lexical date order. Once a recipe has been shared with canary users, do not rewrite its migration meaning.
statement: In the codemod archive, recipes must live under .agents/skills/codemod/codemods/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/ and shared recipes must not be rewritten (add a later corrective recipe).

quote: Rename unmerged work-in-progress symbols: update the source and current in-repository call sites directly. Do not manufacture a migration archive for an API no consumer could have used.
statement: For unreleased APIs, codemod recipes must not be created; only APIs on the default branch or released get archived codemods.

quote: `Text` and `TextGroup` never accept handle or root props.
statement: In the React adapter, Text and TextGroup components must not accept handle or root props; both come from the immutable Glyph React context.

quote: `loadFont`, `createFontLibrary`, `FontLibrary`, and a public font-library subpath are not part of the React or root API.
statement: In the React and root entries, loadFont, createFontLibrary and FontLibrary must not be exported, and no public font-library subpath may exist.

quote: The Glyph FontFace graph is the sole semantic cache for source bytes, decoded formats, dependencies, and renderer resources.
statement: In React and Vue adapters, code must not create another byte, decoded-font, shaping or renderer-resource cache beside the FontFace graph.

quote: The composables read the Glyph context of the nearest `GlyphProvider`, otherwise the canvas-local default root, so they must run inside a `<TresCanvas>` subtree; `preloadFont` and `clearFont` do not read a context and may run at module scope.
statement: In Vue consumers, useFont and the format composables must be called inside a TresCanvas subtree; only preloadFont/clearFont may be called at module scope.

quote: The Three classes are registered in the Tres catalogue under private names only so the custom renderer can construct and dispose them. Applications use the wrapper components; the tags are not public.
statement: In Vue applications, code should use the Text/TextGroup wrapper components rather than the private Tres catalogue tags.

quote: The view and every borrowed sequence or byte slice inside it expire when `decode()` returns. Copy scalar values and retain schema-produced object identities as needed; never store the view, its sequences, or patch payloads.
statement: In GlyphRenderer.decode implementations, the CommandBufferView, its sequences and patch payloads must not be stored beyond the call; copy scalars instead.

quote: Do not cache by display names or filenames.
statement: In renderer integrations, resources must not be cached by display names or filenames; use Glyph's resolved resource identities and generations.

quote: They do not rediscover hierarchy: `DisplayList.children` already interleaves batches and root instances in authoritative order.
statement: In schema batch/instance callbacks, code should not rediscover hierarchy; use DisplayList.children order.

quote: | Shader | Optional explicit TypeGPU/TSL/WGSL/GLSL subpath | Never imports shader code |
statement: In Glyph core (renderer-neutral) code, shader code must never be imported.

quote: | Material/pipeline | May provide a language-level helper | Never owns GPU objects |
statement: In Glyph core code, GPU objects (materials, pipelines) must never be owned; the renderer integration creates and caches them.

quote: Keep TypeGPU, TSL, WGSL, or GLSL code behind explicit subpaths so unused shader implementations do not enter the bundle.
statement: In raster-format packages, TypeGPU, TSL, WGSL or GLSL shader code must live behind explicit shader subpaths, not the main format entry.

quote: portable authors do not choose buffer IDs, interleaving, attributes, storage, or bind groups.
statement: In portable raster Codec bodies, code must not choose buffer IDs, interleaving, attributes, storage or bind groups.

quote: Its production code may import the root package, its portable raster package, and the raster's explicit `/typegpu` shader subpath. It may not import package internals, generated readers, or Three.
statement: In packages/glyph-example-renderer/src/**, code must import only @pmndrs/glyph, the example raster package and its /typegpu subpath, never Glyph internals, generated readers or Three.

quote: Import integration contracts from `@pmndrs/glyph`, never a removed `/core` entry or private file.
statement: In packages/glyph-example-renderer, integration contracts must be imported from @pmndrs/glyph, never a private file.

quote: Import shader implementations only from an explicit raster-format shader subpath.
statement: In packages/glyph-example-renderer, shader implementations must be imported only from an explicit raster-format shader subpath.

quote: Keep the package independent of Three and R3F.
statement: In packages/glyph-example-renderer, code must not import three or @react-three/fiber.

quote: Decode transactionally and preserve the previous accepted state on failure.
statement: In the example renderer's decode, code must stage changes transactionally and preserve the previous accepted state on failure.

quote: Make a missing public capability fail visibly rather than adding a private import or corrective cast.
statement: In the example renderer, a missing public capability must fail visibly rather than be worked around with a private import or corrective cast.

quote: Keep physical device, canvas, context, render-pass, and submission ownership in the host integration.
statement: In renderer integrations, physical device, canvas, context, render-pass and submission ownership must stay in the host integration, not Glyph.

quote: It imports only published `@pmndrs/glyph` entry points and optional shader-language subpaths. ... A source boundary test rejects imports from core internals or the Three first-party raster and baker subpaths.
statement: In packages/glyph-example-raster/src/**, code must import only published @pmndrs/glyph entry points, never core internals or the first-party Three raster/baker subpaths.

quote: Importing the package root runs the renderer-neutral `registerRasterCodec` call through a dedicated registration module. The manifest marks that module and its root facade as side-effectful ... the portable definition and shader subpaths remain free of registration side effects.
statement: In raster-format packages, registerRasterCodec must run only in a dedicated registration module listed as side-effectful in package.json; the portable definition and shader subpaths must have no registration side effects.

quote: The `/typegpu` and `/tsl` subpaths export shader functions and the same named-input descriptor; they do not register a renderer or own resource/material caches.
statement: In raster shader subpaths (/typegpu, /tsl), code must not register a renderer or own resource/material caches.

quote: The analytic Slug fill algorithm lives in `src/shaders/typegpu/slug/core` as TypeGPU shader functions over plain values, and nothing in that directory imports a renderer.
statement: In packages/glyph/src/shaders/typegpu/slug/core/**, code must not import any renderer.

quote: The root entry has no static edge to the baker, its `std`-enabled dependencies, Ajv, glTF Validator, or the baker Wasm; only explicit bake/runtime-bake surfaces can load those bytes.
statement: In the @pmndrs/glyph root entry graph, code must not statically import the baker, Ajv, glTF Validator or baker Wasm; only /bake and /runtime-bake may load them.

quote: `typegpu` is an optional peer and the root entry has no static edge to it.
statement: In the @pmndrs/glyph root entry graph, code must not statically import typegpu.

quote: TypeScript does not independently shape, lay out, or pack paragraphs.
statement: In TypeScript sources, code must not independently shape, lay out or pack paragraphs; that belongs to the Rust/Wasm engine.

quote: The benchmark-only font asset module is the sole test-instrumentation exception to the application FontFace path. ... benchmark call sites import only the harness-owned `loadBenchmarkFont` operation.
statement: In benches/**, only the benchmark font asset module may call Glyph's private loader; other benchmark call sites must use loadBenchmarkFont.

quote: Koota does not enter `@pmndrs/glyph`, shaping, layout, baking, raster packages, or their public contracts.
statement: In @pmndrs/glyph and raster packages, code must not import koota; Koota is used only at the benchmark application boundary.

quote: The world instance lives in a dedicated module so React Fast Refresh of component modules does not allocate a replacement world.
statement: In benches/**, the Koota world instance must be created in a dedicated module, not in a component module.

quote: The complete JavaScript surface is ESM-only. `@pmndrs/glyph` and every public subpath publish ESM exports without a CommonJS build or `require` condition.
statement: In all packages, code must be ESM-only: no CommonJS build, require() or module.exports, and no require export condition.

quote: `import()` is the only lazy-loading mechanism for the runtime baker, generators, optional raster engines, and transcoders.
statement: In packages/glyph, the runtime baker, generators, optional raster engines and transcoders must be lazy-loaded only via dynamic import().

quote: Node-only imports remain reachable only from the bake host and CLI subpath, never from the browser-safe core graph.
statement: In packages/glyph, Node-only imports (node:*) must be reachable only from the bake host and CLI subpath, never from the browser core graph.

quote: A baked asset hit must not make the main module graph reach the runtime baker library or generator modules.
statement: In packages/glyph, the main module graph must not statically reach the runtime baker library or generator modules.

quote: A subpath owns its concepts, exports its contracts, and consumes other subpaths only through their public entries — enforced by lint (D-249)
statement: In packages/glyph, each subpath must consume other subpaths only through their public entries, not their internals.

quote: | `@pmndrs/glyph/core` | engine host, frame wire, plan view, policy authoring, binding compiler | any renderer, any shader language |
statement: In the @pmndrs/glyph/core subpath, code must not import any renderer or shader language.

quote: | `@pmndrs/glyph/raster/<t>` | **the technique declaration** (this plan's construct) | Three, TSL node graphs |
statement: In raster technique declaration modules, code must not import Three or TSL node graphs.

quote: | `@pmndrs/glyph/bakers/<t>` | artifact production and validation | rendering |
statement: In baker modules, code must not import rendering code.

quote: | `@pmndrs/glyph` | fonts, text, styles, runtime | GPUs, shaders, plans |
statement: In the @pmndrs/glyph root entry, code must not depend on GPU, shader or plan modules.

quote: shader realizations are per-language, schemas are per-technique, and they must not be the same file.
statement: In packages/glyph, shader realizations and technique schemas must live in separate files.

quote: First-party integration rigor is enforced by a scoped `no-restricted-imports` lint denying the three, tsl, and react surfaces any import from `internal/` or `generated/`.
statement: In packages/glyph three, tsl and react surfaces, code must not import from internal/ or generated/ modules.

quote: Effects remain external-system synchronization; effect-only events use `useEffectEvent`, never render-time ref reads.
statement: In React components, effects must be used only for external-system synchronization, and effect-only events must use useEffectEvent rather than render-time ref reads.

quote: Applications and ordinary renderer code never author or consume the engine's numeric IDs.
statement: In applications and renderer integrations, code must not author or consume the engine's numeric IDs.

quote: Those types remain private implementation machinery where useful, but they are not an integration surface and must not appear in examples, package exports, or third-party adapters.
statement: In examples, package exports and third-party adapters, the superseded engine construction, binding owner, planning and target types must not appear.

quote: Material creation runs while Three holds borrowed plan-backed attributes. It must return synchronously and must not query or update text
statement: In Three material factories (create()), code must return synchronously and must not query or update text.

quote: For a Text-local glyph measurement, multiply `originalMatrix` by the Text's `matrixWorld` to get its world transform; do not add `anchorOffset` again.
statement: In code using Text-local glyph measurements, anchorOffset must not be added again; multiply originalMatrix by matrixWorld.

quote: never imports uikit, Yoga, or Preact Signals from core.
statement: In Glyph core, code must not import uikit, Yoga or Preact Signals.

quote: Core type tests must not import or mention TSL, TypeGPU, shader-node, WebGPU-pipeline, or WebGL-material types.
statement: In core type tests, code must not import or mention TSL, TypeGPU, shader-node, WebGPU-pipeline or WebGL-material types.

quote: It must compile using only documented package exports and a gpucat peer dependency. It must not import `@pmndrs/glyph/src/*`, workspace-relative source, or an engine-specific core subpath.
statement: In the @pmndrs/glyph-gpucat fitness package, code must not import @pmndrs/glyph/src/*, workspace-relative source or engine-specific core subpaths.

quote: `Text.readGlyphs(callback)` replaces `withGlyphs(callback)` across the shared controller, Three and TypeGPU entries. ... No old-name alias ships.
statement: In package and consumer code, the synchronous borrowed glyph read must be named readGlyphs; withGlyphs must not be used or aliased.

quote: `Text.split()` replaces `Text.breakApart()` ... No old-name alias is published.
statement: In package and consumer code, detached text copies must use Text.split(); breakApart must not be used or aliased.

quote: Package-owned span arrays and records are frozen before they are trusted.
statement: In text compilers and framework adapters, package-owned span arrays and records must be frozen before provenance is attached and trusted.

quote: It publishes native ESM only; optional React, baker, runtime-bake, and raster capabilities live behind explicit subpaths or dynamic imports.
statement: In @pmndrs/glyph, optional React, baker, runtime-bake and raster capabilities must live behind explicit subpaths or dynamic imports, not the root graph.

quote: heterogeneous registries expose associated values as `unknown` and must narrow before technique-specific operations. No public helper silently degrades a failed inference to `any`.
statement: In raster technique registries, associated values must be exposed as unknown and narrowed before technique-specific use; public helpers must not degrade failed inference to any (no RasterTechnique<any, ...>).

quote: The rule that made the change tractable is that identifiers move and string literals do not
statement: In API renames, identifiers are renamed but string literals (artifact kinds, schema enums, fixture filenames, URL vocabulary) must not be changed.
